picks.intervention_label: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, standard STS dosing (not osteosarcoma-type MAP)
picks.rationale: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy is the only systemic option with response data in her actual histology: ORR 20.5% in the dedifferentiated subset of the French Sarcoma Group cohort (n=180), with the modern five-centre series (ORR 9%, metastatic median OS 7.2 months) as the honest floor. Doxorubicin also has four decades of safety follow-up, a cardiotoxicity ceiling everyone knows how to monitor, and febrile-neutropenia pathways that work at any community site. I would give it as standard STS therapy and not as osteosarcoma-type MAP: EURO-B.O.S.S. is uncontrolled and fitness-selected, and the comparative datasets (SEER HR 0.75, pooled OR 1.25) find no survival edge to pay for the added toxicity. Nothing starts until an echo, organ-function labs and a measured ECOG exist; with PS >=2 independently predicting shorter PFS, that measurement is prognosis, not paperwork.
primary_concerns: Baseline cardiac function is unknown; anthracycline cannot start without an LVEF, and no organ-function labs exist either.
If the measured ECOG is truly 2, expected PFS shortens (PS >=2 independently prognostic in pmid 24099780) and the benefit case thins.
None of the retrospective cohorts reports per-term AE rates, so the grade distribution for this specific population is inferred from general doxorubicin experience, not measured in it.

picks.intervention_label: IDH1/IDH2 hotspot testing on a comprehensive DNA/RNA panel
picks.rationale: This is the rare move in the case with no safety cost at all: IDH1/2 mutations run 71% in dedifferentiated versus 36% in conventional disease, and one hotspot assay (3-10 day turnaround) or the comprehensive panel gates ivosidenib, the IDH trial family and every genotype-matched protocol at once. A blood-and-block order does not usually make a tumor-board ranking, but in a case where nothing is measured it is the highest-yield, lowest-harm act available. Expectations stay tempered even if it returns positive: the ivosidenib ORR of 23.1% belongs to the 13-patient conventional subset, and olutasidenib in dedifferentiated disease managed a median PFS of 1.5 months. Test the primary and, where feasible, a metastasis, because mutant IDH1 is recurrently lost in metastatic evolution.
primary_concerns: A positive result opens options whose benefit in her subtype is unquantified; it must not delay first-line chemotherapy.
Archival pelvic tissue may not describe the lung nodules (pmid 41299743); tissue choice needs stating on the requisition.

picks.intervention_label: Orthopaedic stabilisation of the acetabular fracture (not oncologic resection)
picks.rationale: Stabilising the fractured acetabulum and resecting the primary are different operations, and I argue only for the first. In dedifferentiated high-grade disease the SEER analysis found no survival association for resection, the Japanese registry's 51.0% versus 19.3% comparison carries a 2-month median in the unresected arm that signals confounding by fitness, and the price of oncologic clearance in the closest pelvic series was hindquarter amputation. Fixation is also the one intervention here that could raise her measured ECOG, which changes prognosis and trial eligibility at the same time. Do it before any radiotherapy: in the fracture-fixation model, irradiated bone healed as atrophic non-union.
primary_concerns: Several protocols carry a 4-week post-surgical washout, so stabilisation has to be sequenced against trial screening deliberately.
No cohort in the dossier reports surgical morbidity; pelvic fixation in metastatic disease has a real complication burden that this literature simply does not measure.
The operative specimen should go to molecular pathology, but the panel must not wait for the operation.

picks.intervention_label: Pembrolizumab, biomarker-conditional, second line
picks.rationale: I hold pembrolizumab in reserve for second line because its safety profile is the best characterised of anything non-cytotoxic in this dossier: over a decade of post-marketing use since the 2014 approval, and irAE algorithms every oncology unit already runs. The chondrosarcoma evidence is genuinely thin (1 responder of 5 in SARC028, 1 PR of 5 in the Bui cohort), so this pick firms up only if PD-L1 on the dedifferentiated component, TMB or MSI comes back supportive. Monotherapy is the version I can defend; the sunitinib-nivolumab bone cohort logged a treatment-related grade 5 pneumonitis and 17% toxicity discontinuation, which is a different risk conversation for an assumed-ECOG-2 patient. The tumour-agnostic TMB-high label is a real if unlikely on-label route after first-line chemotherapy.
primary_concerns: PD-L1 prevalence of 41-52% in dedifferentiated tumours is prevalence, not response prediction.
Chondrosarcoma is typically TMB-low, so the on-label pembrolizumab route is a long shot that costs nothing to test but should not be planned around.
All efficacy data are single-arm or retrospective; there is no PFS estimate to schedule a second line against.

picks.intervention_label: TAPUR: marketed targeted agents by genomic match (NCT02693535)
picks.rationale: TAPUR assigns marketed agents by genomic match, which means known toxicity profiles and existing management algorithms rather than a novel mechanism, and its ECOG 0-2 bar is one of very few in the whole screen she may clear as written. Everything about it is conditional on the pending panel, and the no-remaining-standard-options language realistically places it after first-line anthracycline. She asked for every option; this one adds protocol structure without adding uncharacterised toxicity, which is why it makes my list ahead of the antigen-directed platforms.
primary_concerns: The panel may find nothing actionable; chondrosarcoma genomes are often quiet beyond IDH.
Any matched agent would be used outside its approved histology, so efficacy in this disease is unknown even where safety is well described.

notes: Two omissions were deliberate, and neither is a veto. Particle therapy is off my list despite the pooled 95% 5-year local control figure, because that number comes from skull-base, non-metastatic cohorts, while the pelvic carbon-ion series reports femoral head necrosis in 37% and insufficiency fracture in 48% of survivors, worst in periacetabular tumours, in a pelvis that has already fractured; the rat data (atrophic non-union after irradiation, pmid 23606416) argue against radiating before the fixation question is settled. If the board wants local RT anyway, it belongs after the orthopaedic decision and after systemic therapy has started, not instead of either. The second omission is osteosarcoma-type MAP intensification, folded into pick 1 as the thing not to do. Her preferences file carries no toxicity vetoes and an 0.8 efficacy weight, so my ordering is not a safety-first override of her stated stance; it reflects what each option charges in time (metastatic dedifferentiated medians run 5 to 7 months across Grimer, Bui and Masunaga) against how certain the return is.

picks.intervention_label: Anthracycline-based chemotherapy, pushed to osteosarcoma-type intensity if measured fitness allows
picks.rationale: The only intervention in this dossier with measured responses in her subtype: ORR 20.5% in dedifferentiated disease against 11.5% conventional (pmid:24099780). My bet goes past what the comparisons prove: EURO-B.O.S.S. put metastatic patients at 29% five-year OS on doxorubicin, ifosfamide and cisplatin (pmid:33990016), against a 5-month median in the surgical-era cohort, and that tail is the only place in this file where anyone is alive at five years. Nobody has shown intensification beats doxorubicin alone (SEER HR 0.75, CI 0.49-1.12), and the EURO-B.O.S.S. cohort was fitness-selected. Measure the real ECOG and the LVEF this week and give her the most intensive regimen she clears; the 5-month median gets spent either way.
primary_concerns: The 29% metastatic five-year OS comes from a fitness-selected uncontrolled cohort; no comparison has ever shown intensification beats doxorubicin alone
Her ECOG 2 is an intake assumption, not a measurement; if the real value is 2 or worse, an intensive regimen may take more than it gives
No baseline LVEF, renal or hepatic panels on file, and all three gate anthracycline and ifosfamide dosing

picks.intervention_label: IACS-6274 (glutaminase-1 inhibitor), phase 1 NCT05039801
picks.rationale: A phase 1 with chondrosarcoma written in as its own dose-escalation population and no prior-therapy requirement is a rare seat, and she can take it as written (nct:NCT05039801). The mechanism fits her tumour specifically: glutaminase expression rises with grade (p=0.001, highest in high-grade disease), and cell-line sensitivity did not track IDH status, so her untested IDH does not gate entry (pmid:29576625). Book the MD Anderson call now and slot enrollment at the first post-chemo decision point. Expected value of phase 1 monotherapy is honestly small; the upside is being the escalation patient the drug turns out to work for.
primary_concerns: ECOG must be 0-1 with no deterioration over the prior fortnight; the assumed 2 has to be measured down before a screening visit is worth booking
Dose-finding design with exploratory efficacy; no chondrosarcoma response has been reported for this class anywhere
The supporting data are in-vitro cytostasis with no in-vivo chondrosarcoma arm

picks.intervention_label: Sunitinib plus nivolumab, off-label at first progression
picks.rationale: The one checkpoint dataset where a dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma actually responded: 1 PR among the 4 dedifferentiated patients in IMMUNOSARC, 6-month PFS 42% (95% CI 27-58) across the bone cohort (pmid:39540661). PD-L1 in chondrosarcoma is confined to her subtype, 9 of 22 dedifferentiated positive against 0 of 119 conventional (pmid:27312065), so the immune argument was built on exactly her histology. Both drugs are marketed, which makes this buyable at first progression without a protocol seat. I will take a 1-in-4 anecdote plus subtype-restricted PD-L1 biology over waiting for trials that exclude her.
primary_concerns: mPFS 3.8 months and ORR 5% overall; the 42% six-month figure is mostly stable disease in a mixed-histology cohort
The dossier's own microenvironment work says macrophages dominate and T-cell depletion accelerated growth in a chondrosarcoma model (pmid:28344871), which argues the PD-1 axis may not be the lever
One treatment-related grade 5 pneumonitis in 40 patients and 17% discontinued for toxicity
Off-label combination, so expect a payer fight

picks.intervention_label: Abemaciclib on NCT04040205, pre-positioned now for the post-anthracycline line
picks.rationale: The clearest post-first-line trial seat in the screen: dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma named by itself, CDKN2A/B loss qualifies, and the one-prior-anthracycline requirement is satisfied by the first-line treatment she should get anyway (nct:NCT04040205). CDKN2A/B loss recurs in this subtype, and palbociclib cut intraosseous chondrosarcoma burden in vivo with the G1 arrest the mechanism predicts (pmid:30808351). The move this week is the comprehensive panel plus Rb IHC, because the biomarker gate cannot be cleared retroactively. A sequencing bet that costs nothing now and buys a named-histology slot most patients in this disease never see.
primary_concerns: ECOG 0-1, stricter than most protocols in the screen; fitness decides this one too
CDK-pathway alteration and Rb status are both untested, so the seat may evaporate on the panel result
Single-arm phase 2 with no chondrosarcoma efficacy data for any CDK4/6 inhibitor yet, and the palbociclib model work never reported CDKN2A status

picks.intervention_label: CD276 (B7-H3) CAR-T on NCT04433221, conditional on a high B7-H3 H-score
picks.rationale: Conditional pick, and the condition is one stain. NCT04433221 gates on antigen expression rather than histology, takes Karnofsky 50% or better with no prior-therapy requirement, the loosest bars in this screen, and B7-H3 CAR-T regressed established osteosarcoma and Ewing xenografts where antigen density was high (pmid:30655315). The prior is against her: chondrosarcoma's median H-score of 60 is the lowest of any sarcoma subtype, but 96% of dedifferentiated tumours express the antigen and nobody has stained hers (pmid:33912442). Order the B7-H3 IHC with an H-score; pursue this only if she reads high, and drop it without regret at the median.
primary_concerns: Density dependence is the central preclinical result and it points away from this histology; a median-range H-score should kill the pick
One site in Shenzhen with safety as the primary endpoint and n=20; travel and self-funding are a hard sell in a 5-month-median disease
Rapidly progressive disease is excluded and lymphodepletion needs fitness nobody has measured
Manufacturing time competes with a tumour that moves in weeks

notes: Two loud options left off on purpose. IDH inhibition: I chase effect size, and the measured effect in dedifferentiated disease is olutasidenib at mPFS 1.5 months (pmid:41895355), with the founder-event biology (pmid:25895133) and recurrent loss of mutant IDH1 in metastases (pmid:41299743) pointing the same way; test IDH anyway, as trial currency, not as a therapy bet. Carbon ion to the pelvis: 37% femoral head necrosis and 48% insufficiency fracture in her exact periacetabular geometry (pmid:32658315), quoted from curative-intent non-metastatic cohorts, while both particle trials exclude distant metastases; toxicity without the survival case is where even I stop. Mifamurtide plus doxorubicin (pmid:40960554) nearly took rank 5, mechanistically the best fit to the macrophage-dominant microenvironment, and lost on the access problem: the EMA label is paediatric osteosarcoma and there is no US route.

picks.intervention_label: Anthracycline-based chemotherapy now; dosing intensity decided with her once fitness is measured
picks.rationale: She asked to pursue all possible therapeutic options, and this is the one that needs no trial seat, no panel result and no prior-authorisation fight: response rates in her histology run from 9% in the modern five-centre cohort to 20.5% in the French Sarcoma Group series. Those numbers, and the 5-to-7-month metastatic medians behind them, have to be said to her out loud before her maximal-options stance can count as informed consent to anything. On dosing I deliberately sit between my colleagues: the 0.8 efficacy weight and the empty veto list are inferred defaults, so neither standard-dose caution nor osteosarcoma-type intensity can be read off her preferences, and the right move is to measure the ECOG and LVEF and then put both regimens with their numbers in front of her. What cannot happen is the assumed ECOG 2 quietly answering an intensity question she was never asked.
primary_concerns: Preference axes: the stated maximal-options stance is fully served (start-now, no access barrier); the efficacy-toxicity weight is unmeasured ground, because the 0.8 is inferred and the intensity trade was never put to her.
PS >=2 independently predicted shorter PFS in the anchor cohort (pmid 24099780), and her 2 is an intake assumption; measuring it changes both the forecast and the dosing conversation.
No LVEF, renal or hepatic baseline exists; anthracycline cannot start without them, so the workup is on the critical path this week.

picks.intervention_label: Comprehensive DNA/RNA panel with full IDH1 codon 132 / IDH2 codon 140/172 coverage, ordered on archival tissue now
picks.rationale: One order is the practical form of her stated preference: the panel opens or closes the IDH axis, the named-histology abemaciclib seat, TAPUR entry and the tumour-agnostic pembrolizumab route all at once, and it rides archival tissue today rather than waiting for any operation. She also deserves the unsaid half of the IDH story: both chondrosarcoma IDH trials exclude her subtype by name, the only published IDH-inhibitor figure in dedifferentiated disease is olutasidenib at a median PFS of 1.5 months, and mutant IDH1 is recurrently lost in metastases. So a positive result buys trial leverage and an off-label conversation, not the targeted rescue the word 'mutation' suggests, and telling her otherwise would be selling false hope. Test the primary, and when an operative or metastatic specimen exists, test that too.
primary_concerns: Preference axes: prefers_trials is served by what the result unlocks; honesty requires saying that NCT06127407 and NCT04278781 exclude dedifferentiated histology no matter what the assay returns.
Panel turnaround runs 2-3 weeks; first-line chemotherapy must not wait for it.

picks.intervention_label: Orthopaedic stabilisation of the acetabular fracture at a high-volume bone-sarcoma centre, timed against trial washouts
picks.rationale: The fracture is the likely source of the assumed ECOG 2, and fixing it is the one intervention on this page that could raise her measured performance status and reopen the trial doors the assumption is currently closing. Be straight about what the operation is: fixation for function, because resection of the primary shows no survival association in her dedifferentiated subgroup and the price of pelvic oncologic clearance in the closest series was hindquarter amputation. Do it at a high-volume bone-sarcoma centre, since that one referral simultaneously buys expert pathology review, the periacetabular surgeons and the trial screens, and centre volume tracks with outcome in pelvic bone sarcoma. Two strings attached: the specimen goes to molecular pathology, since it is the largest sample she will ever produce, and the 4-week post-surgical washout on several protocols means the operative date gets picked with the trial calendar open.
primary_concerns: Preference axes: modality_constraints is empty because nobody asked; the burden of pelvic surgery in metastatic disease was never discussed with her and its morbidity is unmeasured in this dossier.
The washout collision is real: stabilisation timed carelessly can cost a trial window in a disease whose metastatic medians run 5 to 7 months.
If pelvic radiotherapy is ever considered, the fixation decision comes first; irradiated bone healed as atrophic non-union in the fracture model (pmid 23606416).

picks.intervention_label: IACS-6274 phase 1 (NCT05039801): make the MD Anderson call this week, enroll only if she chooses it knowing the numbers
picks.rationale: The single open protocol in the whole screen that writes chondrosarcoma in as its own treatment-naive dose-escalation population, which makes it the literal test of pursuing all possible therapeutic options: the phone call costs nothing and should happen this week. Honesty first, though: no glutaminase inhibitor has a chondrosarcoma clinical result anywhere, the ECOG bar is 0-1 against her assumed 2, and taking a phase 1 monotherapy slot first-line would spend her only proven-response window on a dose-finding question. My advocacy is for the call and the screening answer, not for delaying anthracycline, unless she hears those numbers and picks the trial anyway. That choice is hers, and today nobody has offered it to her.
primary_concerns: Preference axes: prefers_trials is served; travel tolerance was never discussed and this is a single-site protocol in Houston.
ECOG 0-1 entry bar with no deterioration over the prior fortnight; the assumed 2 has to be measured, and measured down, before screening is worth the trip.
The supporting evidence is cell-line work showing grade-dependent glutaminase expression (pmid 29576625); expected benefit from escalation-phase monotherapy is honestly small.

picks.intervention_label: TAPUR (NCT02693535), pre-positioned for the line after first-line chemotherapy
picks.rationale: TAPUR's ECOG 0-2 bar is one of the very few in the screen her assumed fitness clears as written, it runs at 181 US sites so geography probably does not bite, and it converts whatever the panel finds into a protocol seat with marketed drugs and known toxicity management. In a disease this fast the second-line decision arrives in months, so pre-positioning the seat now is what her trials-forward stance looks like in practice. Everything is conditional on the panel finding something actionable, which chondrosarcoma genomes often decline to do, and she should hear plainly that this seat may never materialise.
primary_concerns: Preference axes: prefers_trials served as written; wholly conditional on the pending panel, and a quiet genome closes it.
Any matched agent would be used outside its approved histology, so efficacy in her disease is unknown even where safety is well described.

notes: What the file actually contains from her is one sentence: she wants to pursue all possible therapeutic options. Every other value, the 0.8 weight, the empty vetoes, the trials-forward flag, is an inferred default, and I ranked accordingly: nothing above narrows her options, and nothing above treats her sentence as consent to a toxicity trade she has not been shown. Two absences to defend. Particle therapy is off my list not because the modality is weak but because the toxicity ledger lands hardest in exactly her anatomy, femoral head necrosis 37% and insufficiency fracture 48% among pelvic survivors with periacetabular tumours faring worst, on a pelvis that is already broken; both particle trials exclude metastatic disease anyway, and carbon ion otherwise means travelling abroad and self-paying when her travel tolerance has never even been asked (pmid 32658315, nct NCT02838602, nct NCT05033288). The B7-H3 and cell-therapy platforms are off because every reachable protocol fails her today on line, histology or fitness, and several have zero chondrosarcoma clinical results; she deserves that said rather than handed a hopeful-sounding list. The referral to a high-volume sarcoma centre has no evidence row I am permitted to rank, so I am putting it here instead: it is the single access step that opens expert pathology review, the periacetabular surgeons, the particle-therapy second opinion and the trial screens at once, and it deserves the same urgency as any drug on this page. One more guard on the ECOG: it is an assumption, and it must not be spent in either direction, neither to justify offering her less than she asked for nor to wave her into intensity she has not been shown the price of. Nobody has measured it, asked her goals of care, or told her the metastatic medians. Until those three conversations happen, every persona at this table, me included, is advocating for a person we have only partly met.

picks.intervention_label: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy at standard soft-tissue-sarcoma dosing (not osteosarcoma-type MAP)
picks.rationale: Everything in this dossier is tier 4 or below and doxorubicin still wins by default, because it is the only thing with a measured response in her histology: two retrospective cohorts, both ROBINS-I Serious, bracketing her expected ORR between 20.5% (dedifferentiated subset, n=44, treated 1988-2011, local investigator response assessment) and 9% (4 PR, 0 CR among the ~43 treated across five centres, 2004-2022). Plan against the 9%. That is the modern series, its first-line regimens were already osteosarcoma-protocol-style, and its metastatic median OS was 7.2 months with 0% alive at five years. Give it as standard STS doxorubicin rather than MAP-type intensification, because the only two comparative estimates anywhere in the file are null (SEER HR 0.75, 0.49-1.12; pooled OR 1.25, 0.80-1.94, I2 2%, n=556), and note that the p=0.04 attached to the 20.5% is a between-subtype comparison, not a test that chemotherapy helped anyone.
primary_concerns: ROBINS-I confounding and classification-of-intervention domains are both Serious here: no protocol, no central response review, heterogeneous regimens, and only 73% anthracycline-containing in the 180-patient cohort, so the exposure being estimated is not a single regimen.
Neither anchor cohort reports one per-term adverse event rate. The toxicity half of the risk-benefit is imported from general doxorubicin experience, not measured in dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma.
PS >=2 was independently associated with shorter PFS in the multivariable model of pmid 24099780, and her ECOG 2 has never been measured. The dose should not be chosen until that number is real.
No LVEF, no renal panel, no hepatic panel on file, and all three set the ceiling on what can be given.

picks.intervention_label: IDH1 codon 132 / IDH2 codon 140-172 sequencing on a comprehensive DNA plus RNA panel
picks.rationale: Order the test, not the belief that travels with it: prevalence data are the cleanest thing in this file (IDH1/2 mutation in 71% of dedifferentiated versus 36% of conventional tumours, macrodissected, n=18 versus 55), turnaround is 3-10 days for a hotspot assay, and it costs her a block. Where the dossier overreaches is the therapeutic inference. Ivosidenib's 23.1% ORR belongs to the 13 conventional-histology patients among the 21 dosed; the 8 non-conventional patients were dosed and their responses were never reported, which is selective outcome reporting rather than absent data, and the successor phase 3 enrols conventional histology only. The one measured figure in her subtype is olutasidenib at mPFS 1.5 months (95% CI 0.2-NR), and the preclinical side agrees: AGI-5198 cut D-2-HG by more than 90% in five endogenously mutant lines while proliferation, migration, global expression, CpG island methylation and H3K4/K9/K27 trimethylation all stayed put to 20 passages, whereas the paper reporting the opposite ran a three-line panel in which HT1080 is a fibrosarcoma.
primary_concerns: A positive result buys trial eligibility, not expected benefit. Anyone quoting 23.1% as her number is quoting a 13-patient conventional-histology subgroup.

Mutant IDH1 is recurrently lost during metastatic evolution (pmid 41299743), so a call on the acetabular primary may not describe the lung nodules. Require the report to state which lesion was sampled.
My high confidence is in the yield of the test, and it does not transfer to any drug sitting behind it.
Nothing about first-line chemotherapy should wait for this result.

picks.intervention_label: Orthopaedic stabilisation of the periacetabular pathologic fracture, not oncologic resection of the primary
picks.rationale: Two rows point in opposite directions and only one of them was analysed in her subgroup. The Japanese propensity-matched registry (2-year DSS 51.0% versus 19.3%, p=0.005) matched on three variables, number of metastatic organs, metastasectomy and chemotherapy, and not on performance status, size or grade; it pooled conventional with dedifferentiated and mesenchymal, and it produced a 2-month median in the unresected arm, which is the signature of selection by fitness rather than of anything surgery prevented. The SEER interaction analysis put the resection benefit in conventional and grade II disease and found no association in dedifferentiated or grade III, and that is a subgroup finding too, so it removes the claim of oncologic benefit without establishing futility. What I rank is fixation of the fracture, and I will say plainly that no cohort in this dossier measured the operation I am endorsing; the argument for it is structural and functional, not an efficacy claim.
primary_concerns: Not one of these series reports surgical morbidity. Pelvic fixation in metastatic disease is not a low-cost intervention and this literature does not count its complications at all.

The closest anatomical match (pelvic dedifferentiated disease, n=31) achieved its margins by hindquarter amputation, and its curative-intent versus palliative comparison is confounded by exactly the fitness gradient that would decide the question.

Fracture and pelvic location were poor prognostic factors in the 337-patient EMSOS cohort but fracture did not affect survival in the 175-patient limb series; the two disagree and neither adjudicates a pelvis.
Four-week post-surgical washouts are standard across protocols, so timing this against trial screening is a real cost rather than a formality.

picks.intervention_label: Pembrolizumab monotherapy, second line, conditional on TMB-high or MSI-high
picks.rationale: Add up the whole prospective checkpoint experience in this disease and it comes to 1 responder of 5 in SARC028, inside a cohort whose primary endpoint was not met (2 of 40) and whose responder's subtype the primary report never states, plus 1 PR of 5 pembrolizumab-treated in a retrospective five-centre series, plus a single case report of a sustained CR. The attribution of that SARC028 responder to dedifferentiated histology is secondhand in later sources, and I will not plan around a citation that traces back to nobody. The microenvironment work argues against the axis rather than for it: macrophages are the dominant population, a high CD68+/CD8+ ratio was independently prognostic (p<0.01, n=76), and in the immunocompetent rat model depleting T cells accelerated growth while depleting CD163+ macrophages slowed it. It keeps a place on my list only because a TMB >=10 or MSI-high call would make it on-label, and the panel that answers that is already going out.
primary_concerns: PD-L1 positivity of 41-52% in dedifferentiated tumours is prevalence, and the one documented responder in the five-centre series was TPS 7% / CPS 8 and microsatellite-stable, so the marker is doing no predictive work in either direction.
The on-label TMB route is a low-prior bet: TMB >=10 mut/Mb appears in 3.9% of sarcomas and chondrosarcoma was not among the ten KEYNOTE-158 cohorts.
Open-label single-arm response ascertainment throughout, with no PFS estimate in this histology against which to schedule a second line.
The 1-of-5 and 1-of-4 numbers everyone cites are subgroups of four and five patients. Their confidence intervals run from roughly nothing to roughly everything.

picks.intervention_label: Abemaciclib on NCT04040205, post-anthracycline, biomarker-gated
picks.rationale: I rank this on the quality of the process rather than on any signal, and the two are not the same thing. No CDK4/6 inhibitor has a published chondrosarcoma efficacy result anywhere; the supporting work is a cell-line plus intraosseous mouse study that never reported CDKN2A status of its lines and needed a 2023 figure correction (pmid 36803557), so the biological case is inference. What the protocol has that almost nothing else in this dossier has is a registered pre-specified primary endpoint, central Rb immunohistochemistry instead of a local read, dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma named as its own eligible histology, and a biomarker gate applied before enrolment rather than after the fact. Her preferences favour trials, first-line anthracycline satisfies the prior-therapy requirement, and the qualifying panel is already on order; ECOG 0-1 is the gate that decides it.
primary_concerns: Single-arm phase 2, n=44 across a mixed sarcoma population. Even a positive readout will not separate drug effect from having selected an indolent CDK-altered subset.
Two untested gates stand in the way, a qualifying CDK-pathway alteration and Rb positivity by central IHC, so the seat may simply not exist for her.
ECOG 0-1 excludes her as currently assumed, which makes this contingent on a measurement nobody has taken.
Nothing here justifies delaying first-line treatment to chase the seat.

notes:
There is no randomised comparison in this dossier for any intervention against any endpoint. Nothing rises above ROBINS-I Serious except a handful of Moderate single-arm phase 1/2 rows, so my ranking orders weak things against each other and should be read that way and not as endorsement. I considered abstaining and did not, because the chemotherapy row is thin evidence for a real option rather than no evidence at all, and a 5-to-7-month median across Grimer, Bui and Masunaga does not leave room to wait for something better designed.

Three declines with the numbers attached. B7-H3: the 96% figure is prevalence off a 24-specimen dedifferentiated TMA with a Merck-employed author, and both the CAR and the ADC literature make efficacy a function of antigen density rather than positivity. Majzner's activity was greatly diminished against low-expressing targets, Barisa showed avidity setting a measurable density threshold, and the only H-score measurement in existence puts chondrosarcoma lowest of any sarcoma subtype at a median of 60 against 175 for osteosarcoma (n=133). No chondrosarcoma patient has received any B7-H3 agent with a published result. One uncalibrated stain cannot carry a ranked pick, and NCT04433221 gives CAR-T with low-dose chemotherapy plus an irradiated tumour-cell vaccine at a single site with n=20 and safety as the primary endpoint, so a response there could not be attributed to the CAR anyway.

Sunitinib plus nivolumab: the 42% six-month PFSR (95% CI 27-58) was tested against a >15% threshold in a four-histology bone cohort, ORR was 5% (2 PR of 38, one of them dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma), and there was one treatment-related grade 5 pneumonitis among 40 with 17% discontinuing for toxicity. A 1-of-4 subgroup is not a rank-3 argument in a patient whose fitness is an assumption.

Particle therapy: the pooled meta-analysis reports 5-year OS of 99% with a confidence interval of 98-101. An interval whose upper bound exceeds 100% is a broken pooling model, and I will not quote effect estimates out of an analysis that produced one. The cohorts are skull-base, non-metastatic and curative-intent; the late-toxicity denominator (n=29) counts survivors only; and the hypoxia half of the carbon-ion rationale failed to replicate, with chronic hypoxia not raising radioresistance and making JJ012 more radiosensitive. I have read abstracts rather than full texts for most of these rows, and where a per-term AE table sits behind a paywall (pmid 33990016) I have said so rather than assumed its contents.

picks.intervention_label: Doxorubicin-based chemotherapy, with or without ifosfamide or cisplatin
picks.rationale: Four personas put anthracycline first before me and I am not going to invent a disagreement. What I can add is an honest guideline read, and it is a narrow one: the two documents that would carry a category here, NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 and Bone sarcomas: ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS-ERN PaedCan Clinical Practice Guideline (Ann Oncol 2021;32:1520-1536), both refused me their full text this pass, so I assert no NCCN category and no ESMO level or grade for doxorubicin in dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma. The dossier numbers are what I am actually ranking on: ORR 20.5% in the dedifferentiated subset of the French Sarcoma Group series against 11.5% in conventional histology, and 9% in the five-centre cohort. Osteosarcoma-type intensification I would describe to her rather than endorse, because EURO-B.O.S.S. reported median OS 24 months (95% CI 22-25) with no comparator arm and both comparative attempts came back null (SEER HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.49-1.12; pooled OR 1.25, 95% CI 0.80-1.94).
primary_concerns: EURO-B.O.S.S. enrolled patients judged fit for intensive chemotherapy; her ECOG 2 is an intake assumption from the fracture and was never measured, so she may sit outside the population that generated the 24-month figure.

Both null comparative datasets (SEER pmid:34648466, pooled review pmid:38275833) are perioperative and localized. Reading them as first-line metastatic evidence is a population swap, in either direction.
No baseline echocardiogram or LVEF has been obtained, and an anthracycline is the one drug class here that requires one first.

picks.intervention_label: Referral to a high-volume bone-sarcoma centre
picks.rationale: This is the pick I would argue hardest for and the one I can document least, which is an uncomfortable place for the guidelines persona to sit. Referral of bone sarcoma to a reference centre is the sentence I went to quote from the ESMO bone sarcoma guideline (Ann Oncol 2021;32:1520-1536, pmid:34500044); the publisher returned HTTP 403 on the full text, and NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 (pmid:40203873) is login-gated the same way, so no grade from me on either. The case-level argument survives without them, because expert bone pathology, periacetabular reconstruction, a particle-therapy opinion and trial screening are all held by the same small set of institutions, and the EMSOS series recorded a median survival of 5 months once chondrosarcoma is metastatic at presentation. The accessibility row says self-referral is accepted at the major centres without a physician letter, which makes this the item on my list that can move today.
primary_concerns: A referral is not a treatment, and ranking it second risks reading as an answer when it is a route to one.
Travel tolerance was never discussed with her; preferences.json says so plainly. A centre 500 miles away with a fractured acetabulum is a different proposition than a centre across town.

Sequencing collision: most protocols impose a 4-week major-surgery washout, and NCT04040205 at 14 days is the exception. Booking surgery and screening for trials at the same centre in the wrong order costs her options.

picks.intervention_label: Periacetabular resection and reconstruction, or orthopaedic stabilisation of the acetabular fracture
picks.rationale: The sequencing question is the one I would settle first: fix or resect before anything irradiates that bone, since the rat model in the dossier produced atrophic non-union after prior irradiation and periosteal stripping, and a non-union in a weight-bearing acetabulum is not recoverable. The fracture itself looks like a structural and functional problem rather than a prognostic one, because in the Rizzoli limb series pathological fracture did not change disease-specific survival (p=0.638). On resection of the primary in already-metastatic chondrosarcoma the two supporting datasets are propensity-matched registry work (2-year DSS 51.0% vs 19.3%, p=0.005) and SEER (HR 0.481), which I read as heavily selected rather than as a mandate. I could not verify what either NCCN or ESMO say about operating on the primary in metastatic bone sarcoma, so I am ranking this on the dossier and on the fracture, not on an endorsement I did not read.
primary_concerns: Internal hemipelvectomy in a patient whose performance status nobody has measured. If the true ECOG is worse than 2, the operation that was supposed to restore her ambulation is the one that ends it.
Everyone who got resected in pmid:40613902 and pmid:30762691 was chosen for resection. Propensity matching on number of metastatic organs does not fix that.
A major pelvic operation delays first-line chemotherapy in a disease whose metastatic median survival is measured in months.

picks.intervention_label: IDH1/IDH2 sequencing within comprehensive DNA/RNA profiling of the dedifferentiated component
picks.rationale: I rank this as workup and as a trial key, not as therapy, and the distinction matters for what she is told. IDH1/2 mutations run at 71% in dedifferentiated chondrosarcoma against 36% in conventional, so the pre-test probability here is high, and the result is what any genotype-matched protocol will ask for first. What it does not buy is ivosidenib: NCT06127407 enrolls conventional histology, the reported dedifferentiated experience with olutasidenib is median PFS 1.5 months, and mutant IDH1 is recurrently lost during metastatic evolution, so a positive result off-trial would be an off-label prescription against a weak biological argument. I could not confirm whether NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 lists IDH testing in the chondrosarcoma workup algorithm, so I am not claiming that it does.
primary_concerns: The sample has to include the dedifferentiated component. Sequencing the cartilaginous part answers a question about a clone that may no longer be driving anything.
Turnaround of two to three weeks against a disease that presents metastatic and moves fast. This has to be sent with the diagnostic tissue, not after the first restaging scan.
A positive IDH1 call will create pressure for off-label ivosidenib. Outside a trial I would not support it here, and I would rather say that now than after the report lands.

picks.intervention_label: Palliative radiotherapy and local measures at the fracture site, with early specialist palliative care alongside
picks.rationale: The one recommendation in this case I read in the original and can quote: the ASCO Palliative Care for Patients With Cancer guideline update (J Clin Oncol 2024) recommends that oncology clinicians refer patients with advanced solid tumours to specialised interdisciplinary palliative care teams. I read the abstract rather than the full recommendation table, so I am not attaching its evidence-quality or strength rating. Alongside that, pain control and weight-bearing at the acetabulum are undocumented in this dossier and are the things she will actually feel, and cementoplasty or percutaneous fixation are available at essentially any interventional service. The caution attached to this row is sequencing again: radiating that acetabulum before the orthopaedic decision is made can foreclose fixation later.
primary_concerns: She said she wants to pursue all possible therapeutic options. Palliative care offered clumsily will be heard as the opposite of that, and it is not.

Palliative-intent radiotherapy to the acetabulum and any definitive local strategy are in direct conflict over the same bone. Radiation oncology and orthopaedic oncology need to decide together, not sequentially by whoever sees her first.

notes: Retrieval was capped deliberately and the ceiling shaped this position. WebSearch was exhausted before I started; I used NCBI E-utilities and Europe PMC, and one direct fetch of the ESMO bone sarcoma guideline PDF that came back HTTP 403. So: NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 (pmid:40203873, JNCCN 2025;23(4):e250017) and Bone sarcomas: ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS-ERN PaedCan Clinical Practice Guideline (pmid:34500044, Ann Oncol 2021;32:1520-1536) are both confirmed to exist and to be the current documents for this disease, and I read neither. No NCCN category and no ESMO level, grade or MCBS score appears anywhere in my rows, which is the whole point. The JNCCN v2.2025 abstract I did read is scoped to Ewing sarcoma and osteosarcoma and says nothing about chondrosarcoma. Particle therapy I declined too, same as every persona ahead of me. Both the comparative carbon-ion pelvic cohort and the proton meta-analysis sit in unresectable non-metastatic disease, both protocol routes exclude distant metastases (NCT02838602, NCT05033288), no operating US carbon-ion facility was verified, and the periacetabular late-toxicity ledger is femoral head necrosis 37%, insufficiency fracture 48% and neurological deficit 52% in a hip that is already fractured. Off-population rather than off-guideline, and I would not fight an insurer for it. Also unranked: pembrolizumab and every other checkpoint route, because MSI, TMB and PD-L1 are all untested and the tumour-agnostic label is what would carry them. The three questions I was asked to answer first, answered plainly: anthracycline is universal practice in this histology but I could not read the category attached to it; osteosarcoma-type intensification has no comparative support in the dossier and I will not call it endorsed; reference-centre referral is the recommendation I most expect to be in both guidelines and least able to prove. Guideline PMIDs verified this run via NCBI esummary (titles, journals, years match). All other identifiers taken from the dossier files.
